Hi Liam — thanks for the questionnaire. We're happy to respond. I've attached a preliminary response doc (Redwood_RFI_Encryption_Responses_v1.docx) with conservative answers and callouts where we need ACME to confirm deployment type (hosted vs private). Quick highlights below to surface the important bits: 

- BYOK: Supported. For Hosted API we integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault for customer-supplied keys; customers can also bring keys via supported import flows. For Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments, customers can configure their own KMS/HSM for master key storage.
- HSM posture: Our hosted root keys are stored in FIPS-validated HSMs (cloud provider HSM offerings). We also support customer-managed HSM appliances for Private deployments; import and wrapping workflows are documented in the attached.
- Envelope encryption: We use envelope encryption for customer data at rest. Data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated per-model/tenant and wrapped with a master key from the configured KMS/HSM.
- Key rotation: Default automated rotation cadence for service-managed master keys is 90 days; DEKs are rotated per lifecycle events. For BYOK customers, rotation is under customer control; we support manual rotation and automated key-version aliasing to minimize disruption.
- TLS: We require TLS 1.2+ and prefer TLS 1.3 for all control and data plane communications; we maintain a strong cipher suite policy and enforce forward secrecy.
- Audit & logs: Key usage and KMS API calls are logged and available via our audit export. We retain audit logs for 3 years by default in hosted plans; retention can be extended for enterprise contracts.

There are a few ACME-specific items we asked clarification on in the doc (e.g., whether you require FIPS 140-2 Level 3-backed HSM appliances for hosted keys vs customer-managed HSMs).

If it's helpful, Rishi can provide a short technical appendix on envelope encryption and the runtime key handling. I'll also coordinate with Legal for any contract-level wording.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Mina / Marissa — brief technical clarifications below that we should fold into the final: 

- Envelope encryption: Confirmed — DEKs are generated per-tenant and per-model shard. DEKs never leave the runtime unencrypted; they are wrapped with a master key (KM) stored in the configured KMS/HSM. For hosted customers who request BYOK, the customer master key is used as the wrapping key.
- BYOK import formats: We support import via PKCS#12 and PEM-wrapped key material for asymmetric keys, and wrapped symmetric key blobs for cloud KMS import. For private deployments, customers can plug in their on-prem HSM via the same wrapping interface.
- HSM levels: Our hosted control plane keys use cloud HSMs that are FIPS-validated; for ACME's L3 preference, we can offer a customer-owned HSM appliance in Private deployments or a dedicated-hosting arrangement (Dedicated pools) where the customer provides the appliance and we handle integration.
- Rotation mechanics: We support zero-downtime rotation via key-version aliasing. New versions are published to the KMS, and the alias atomically flips; the runtime lazily rewraps DEKs on first access to avoid mass rewrap spikes.
- Auditability: All KMS API calls and key unwrap/wrap events are emitted to our audit stream and can be exported (Syslog/S3/GCS). We include request IDs and token-level traces to map usage back to tenant requests for forensics.

I'll clean up these bullets into a short appendix section — happy to pair on the final PDF.

— Rishi

Liam / ACME security team — thanks for the follow-up. Attached is our consolidated and final response (Redwood_RFI_Encryption_Final_ACME.pdf). Highlights:

- BYOK & HSM: We support BYOK across major cloud KMS vendors and allow customer-managed HSM appliances for Private/Dedicated deployments. For hosted keys we use FIPS-validated cloud HSMs; customers seeking FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware can opt for a Dedicated + customer-provided appliance integration.
- Key lifecycle & rotation: Envelope encryption with DEKs wrapped by master keys in the configured KMS. Rotation is supported via key-version aliasing; default rotation cadence for service-managed keys is 90 days; BYOK rotation schedule is customer-controlled.
- TLS & ciphers: TLS 1.2 minimum; TLS 1.3 preferred. We enforce modern cipher suites with forward secrecy and maintain a routine vulnerability patching schedule.
- Audit & retention: KMS and key-usage audit logs are exportable. Default hosted retention is 3 years; we can contractually extend retention or provide on-prem archival for enterprise agreements.

Open item: ACME noted a preference for L3 HSM for hosted master keys. Our current hosted offering relies on cloud-provider HSMs (FIPS-validated), and we can provide an integration path for customer-owned L3 appliances in Dedicated/Private setups. Would you like us to draft the operational runbook for an L3 appliance integration?

Next step: if the above looks acceptable, could you confirm the procurement contact we should send the SOW and pricing to? We can also schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through with Rishi and your security engineers.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
